commenti.body:
Uggghhhhh this is a beautiful and narratively immaculate addition to a story which I see as criminally underrated (despite its young age). I posted on here when the movie first came out that it's a guide book on gratitude. It wants viewers to understand and practice that which it displays. The film is a wholesome and loving beast for that alone.

The one point of debate I've seen around this film is on his backstory, and you've laid that to rest quite eloquently by sharing this. I can not wait to refer back to your points in future conversations, thank you so much for sharing this.

You just brought this to my mind; the line "now is now" is so true and simple yet also dismissive and veiled. She's your niece. Make a fkn plan with her. But the best lesson that he can pass to someone in her shoes is just a sliver of momentary gratitude from his life. Relax and look at the leaves, you might need this more than you know.

Awesome tidbits, thanks for this. As a recovering alcoholic/drug addict who’s been in and out of recovery for 8 years now, this adds even more substance to a film I thought was amazing and emotionally captivating, elevating it to an even more personal level. 

I appreciate you sharing this OP!
I’m so glad you found them useful!!

You do get the sense that she looks to him for answers about how to find a way out from their family dynamics. She also introduces a potential for further changes—whatever they may be—in Hirayama by finding her way into his pictures of light and trees. She’s the only human in these pictures.
